stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $281M C-PACE Loan for Boston Condos
stories.excerpt: The steady climb of commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) financing around the U.S. has made its way to one of Boston’s tallest buildings. Millennium Partners has secured a $281 million C-PACE loan to implement energy efficiency upgrades at the 62-story Winthrop Center in Downtown Boston, the developer announced Friday afternoon. Nuveen Green Capital originated the fixed-rate loan under the Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Massachusetts program which marked the largest C-PACE financing to date in the New England region, according to the lender.,. The condo inventory of the roughly 800,000 square-foot mixed-use building completed in 2023 attracted strong lender competition with many debt funds chasing the loan, according to a source familiar with the transaction. The C-PACE debt closed concurrently with a $575 million commercial mortgage backed securities (CMBS) loan led by Morgan Stanley for the office and retail portion of the tower according to a presale report from Moody’s. CoStar first reported the MP Trust 2026-WTRP single-asset-single-borrower deal for Boston’s largest building in the city’s financial district. The combined $856 million debt package takes out a prior construction loan from Cale Street in October 2020 after the London firm stepped in following another bank who backed out during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, according to sources. “We were honored to partner with MassDevelopment to recapitalize the largest C-PACE-financed project in New England, one that has helped reshape downtown Boston with state-of-the-art, energy-efficient residences,” Mike Doty, senior director of originations for NGC, said in a statement. Christopher M. Jeffries, founder of Millennium Partners, said in a statement that the C-PACE loan “recognizes the investments we have made in energy efficiency while providing long-term capital that supports the building’s enduring performance.” The PACE Massachusetts program was updated in June
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closed $281M C-PACE loan for Millennium Partners' Winthrop Center, Boston.
Largest C-PACE financing in New England; mixed-use 62-story building with 317 luxury condos completed 2023.
Strong lender competition; concurrent $575M CMBS loan from Morgan Stanley signals refinance strength.
stories.summary: Millennium Partners secured $281 million in Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing from Nuveen Green Capital for energy efficiency upgrades at Boston's Winthrop Center, a 62-story mixed-use development completed in 2023 containing 317 luxury condominium residences. The loan is the largest C-PACE financing to date in New England and closed concurrently with a $575 million CMBS loan led by Morgan Stanley. Strong lender competition for the deal underscores robust debt market appetite for completed, stabilized luxury residential assets with condo inventory.
stories.impact: Rising availability of permanent, lower-cost C-PACE refinancing tools signals improved financing pathways for mixed-use residential developments in Northeast markets. For future Boston and New England deals, C-PACE recapitalization extends financing terms and lowers cost of capital on residential components, improving dev returns and creating competitive advantage in feasibility; establishes precedent for $250M+ structures in region.

stories.title: CEDARst Closes on Construction Loan for Sixth San Diego Multifamily
stories.excerpt: CEDARst Companies has closed on construction financing and launched construction on a 197-unit multifamily development, The Samuel, located at the corner of Adams Avenue and Idaho Street in San Diego’s North Park neighborhood. CrossHarbor Capital Partners provided an $80,000,000 construction loan for the project. JLL Capital Markets, led by Zach Kersten, arranged the financing. KPRS Construction Services is serving as general contractor. The development will feature 189 parking spaces and a full suite of resident amenities. “North Park continues to be one of San Diego’s most in-demand submarkets, and this project reflects our commitment to delivering thoughtfully designed, amenity-forward housing in infill locations,” said Will Murphy, CEO, CEDARst Companies. “We’re grateful for the partnership with CrossHarbor and KPRS as we move this project into vertical construction.” The Samuel adds to four other CEDARst projects under development in San Diego and one stabilized asset. A September 2028 completion date is expected for the property. The post CEDARst Closes on Construction Loan for Sixth San Diego Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CEDARst closed $80M construction loan from CrossHarbor Capital for 197-unit North Park, San Diego.
The Samuel at Adams/Idaho; 189 parking spaces; September 2028 delivery in high-demand infill submarket.
Sixth CEDARst project in San Diego pipeline; demonstrates lender confidence in North Park thesis.
stories.summary: CEDARst Companies closed $80 million in construction financing from CrossHarbor Capital Partners for The Samuel, a 197-unit multifamily development in San Diego's North Park neighborhood at Adams Avenue and Idaho Street. JLL Capital Markets arranged the loan. The project features 189 parking spaces and full amenity suite with an expected September 2028 completion. This is CEDARst's sixth San Diego project underway, with four additional developments and one stabilized asset in the pipeline.
stories.impact: Continued North Park absorption of infill multifamily at scale—197 units in a highly sought submarket—signals sustained rental demand in central San Diego. Lender willingness to commit $80M to sixth consecutive CEDARst project in same metro indicates confidence in both developer execution and persistent North Park rent growth; signals window for competing infill sites in North Park and adjacent Hillcrest/University Heights submarkets may narrow as supply tightens.

stories.title: Winthrop Center Residences Secure New England’s Largest C-PACE Financing
stories.excerpt: MassDevelopment, Nuveen Green Capital and Millennium Partners announced $281 million in private financing for the Millennium Residences at Winthrop Center at 115 Federal St. in downtown Boston under the state’s Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Massachusetts program. This project is believed to represent the largest commercial PACE financing to date in New England. Developed and owned by Millennium Partners, Winthrop Center combines the world’s largest Passive House office building with public gathering spaces and 317 luxury condominium residences. Through PACE Massachusetts, Millennium Partners will recapitalize and extend the financing term for The Millennium Residences at Winthrop Center using permanent, lower-cost financing from Nuveen Green Capital and will repay the financing via a betterment assessment on the property. “This historic financing for Winthrop Center will help residents and businesses lower their bills by reducing their energy usage, while supporting continued economic growth in downtown Boston,” said Gov. Maura Healey. “Through PACE Massachusetts, we’re bringing private investment to the table to support major developments and make our buildings cleaner and more efficient.” The post Winthrop Center Residences Secure New England’s Largest C-PACE Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Millennium Partners secured $281M PACE Massachusetts financing for Winthrop Center, Downtown Boston.
Largest New England C-PACE deal; permanent lower-cost structure for 317 luxury condo residences.
Gov. Healey cited economic growth support; recapitalization extends financing term on stabilized asset.
stories.summary: MassDevelopment, Nuveen Green Capital, and Millennium Partners announced $281 million in permanent PACE Massachusetts financing for Millennium Residences at Winthrop Center (115 Federal Street, downtown Boston). The deal, believed to be the largest commercial PACE financing in New England, will recapitalize and extend the financing term for the 317-unit luxury condo component of the mixed-use, 62-story Passive House office building completed in 2023. Repayment occurs via betterment assessment on the property.
stories.impact: Replicates story #1 with added state policy angle: PACE Massachusetts program explicitly marketed as tool to support major developments and economic growth. For multifamily developers, demonstrates state willingness to use public PACE infrastructure to unlock refinance liquidity on residential components; creates precedent for applying permanent PACE capital to future Boston residential deals, particularly mixed-use projects seeking extended financing terms.

stories.title: Developer Proposes 600+ Mixed-Income Apartments in Bronx’s Soundview Neighborhood
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn-based Heights Advisors has filed a land use application to build 606 mixed-income apartments in the Soundview section of the Bronx. The 21-story, 515,000-quare-foot mixed-use building at 945 White Plains Rd. would rise on a site currently occupied by a low-rise retail building housing Modell’s Sporting Goods and GameStop, according to published reports. The application launches New York City’s mandatory Uniform Land Use Review Procedure, entailing public review before the project can move forward. Heights Advisors is reportedly seeking financing through the Department of Housing Preservation & Development’s New Construction Finance program, which is geared toward 100% affordable developments. The project is being positioned as a large multifamily development with a significant affordable housing component. If the project goes ahead, the 945 White Plains Rd. development would add to other proposed residential construction in the vicinity, along with expanding the availability of income-restricted housing in the Bronx. stories.summary: Brooklyn-based Heights Advisors filed a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) application to develop 606 mixed-income apartments in the Soundview section of the Bronx at 945 White Plains Road, a 515,000-square-foot, 21-story mixed-use building on a site currently occupied by low-rise retail (Modell's Sporting Goods, GameStop). The developer is seeking financing through HPD's New Construction Finance program, which targets 100% affordable developments. If approved, the project would add significant income-restricted housing stock to the Bronx alongside other residential construction in the vicinity.
stories.impact: Large-scale (606-unit) infill redevelopment on Soundview retail site signals supply response to acute Bronx affordable housing shortage; HPD financing availability suggests municipal willingness to subsidize multifamily in emerging submarkets. For market participants: Soundview's transformation from retail-dominated to residential-dense is underway; window for acquiring additional infill retail/commercial sites in submarket for conversion may remain open but closing—early-mover advantage shrinking as Heights Advisors and other developers activate pipeline.

stories.title: Entre Commercial Realty Completes 21K-SF Lease in Wauconda
stories.excerpt: Entre Commercial Realty completed the lease of a 20,500 square foot industrial building located at 1275 Kyle Court in Wauconda, Illinois. The freestanding industrial facility features 20-foot clear heights, two exterior loading docks, and one drive-in door. Brian Bocci, SIOR, and Jack Steineke of Entre Commercial represented the landlord in the transaction. Prior to the lease, Bocci also represented the seller in the sale of the property to an investment purchaser. Shortly after the acquisition, they successfully secured a tenant, completing the investor’s lease-up strategy and bringing the building to full occupancy. Cawley Commercial Real Estate represented the tenant in the lease transaction. “This transaction demonstrates the value of providing clients with full-cycle real estate services, from investment sales to leasing,” said Brian Bocci, SIOR. “We are proud to have helped our client acquire the property as an investment and quickly secure a quality tenant.” Join the Executives Driving Western Industrial Real Estate | August 20Hear from senior leaders representing the industry’s most active firms as they discuss investment strategy, market fundamentals, leasing trends, and emerging opportunities across the West Coast. stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
stories.excerpt: Fancy a trip to the Boardwalk? A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. For NYC developers: Coney Island waterfront re-emerging as viable development opportunity; Brooklyn coastal submarkets showing capital return after period of caution—watch for financing announcements to confirm construction readiness.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said
bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of investors hold negative multifamily outlook for H2 2026; 52% underperformed H1 2026 expectations.

stories.summary: In a Berkadia survey of over 100 principals and executives at private real estate investment firms, 61 percent characterized their outlook for multifamily in H2 2026 as negative, citing capital markets volatility, interest rate uncertainty, and softer-than-expected property performance. Fifty-two percent said the asset class performed worse in H1 2026 than anticipated. The 10-Year Treasury is at 4.7 percent (highest since 2023) and the 30-Year Treasury at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. Investors had been optimistic six months ago that volatility would fade and transaction activity would accelerate, but instead the operating environment has remained uncertain.
stories.impact: Broad-based investor pessimism on multifamily fundamentals creates risk for active development portfolios heading into 2H 2026: higher cap rates, stricter underwriting, reduced leverage availability, and slower exit liquidity all compress development returns. Persistent 4.7%+ 10Y Treasury yields make construction financing expensive and prolong carry costs. For new acquisitions and starts: window for favorable underwriting narrowing; developers should focus on markets with concrete job growth and rent-up visibility rather than speculative infill. Capital may consolidate toward stabilized assets and experienced sponsors; emerging developers face capital constraints.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinanced St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort $263M after special servicing; assumed $188M existing debt.
213-room hotel; 2024 cash flow ~50% of 2021 levels; asset valued at $311M; oceanfront Bal Harbour, Florida.
Original CMBS lender Column Financial moved loan to special servicing over interest rate cap dispute; resort remained current.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company's St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort from special servicing, providing a $263 million refinance loan. Fortress assumed $188 million in existing CMBS debt and added $70 million in new capital, valuing the 213-room oceanfront property at $311 million in Bal Harbour, Florida (north of Miami Beach). The property had been in special servicing after its original $188 million CMBS loan matured; while the loan remained current and debt service coverage stayed above break-even, 2024 cash flow was roughly 50 percent of 2021 levels, and the servicer sought an interest rate cap replacement that the owner had not secured.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Hospitality (hotel) asset in South Florida, not residential. However, signals broader capital market stress: distressed hospitality refinances driven by cap rate expansion and underperformance cascade; South Florida (including Miami and Bal Harbour) tourism/hospitality weakness may reflect softer inbound migration and job growth than bullish narrative suggests, which could dampen regional multifamily fundamentals if leisure/tourism sectors contract further.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquired Queens retail center (Bayside) for $23.5M from Levy Properties.
213-04 Northern Boulevard; 24K SF built space, 74.35K SF air rights; currently urgent care and baby store.
Property features 98.478K total buildable SF; multifamily development pipeline active in Queens.
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners Real Estate acquired a one-story retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, from Levy Properties for $23.5 million. The property contains 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total buildable area of 98,478 square feet. The center currently houses an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Buyer intentions remain unclear, though Queens has seen substantial multifamily development activity.
stories.impact: Retail-to-residential conversion opportunity flagged: First Pioneer's acquisition of 98.5K buildable-SF Bayside retail site with substantial air rights suggests positioning for multifamily redevelopment. Queens multifamily pipeline remains active (concurrent Wells Fargo $175M construction loan noted in article); Bayside is emerging residential submarket. For developers: retail distress in outer boroughs creates conversion opportunities; air rights availability lowers density constraints. Monitor First Pioneer's next moves—timing of entitlement filing and lender interest will signal Bayside's continued attractiveness vs. other Queens submarkets (Flushing, Astoria, Long Island City).
